reviewedBoundaries: Raw output parent spelling reaches native realpath before path normalization. Canonical output/repository overlap rejects both ancestor directions before native collection.
Both existing or dangling report/journal leaves reject before creation. Exclusive opens protect against a leaf created after the precheck.
Separate retained report and append-mode journal descriptors eliminate pathname reopen during writes.
Held/named identity, link count, mode, size and observed timestamps are checked around writes and at finish. Repository and parent identities are rechecked.
Partial writes, creation collisions and replacements retain owned evidence without deleting a raced pathname. A failure closes both descriptors where possible and keeps the original error primary.
The 16 MiB journal limit preserves the verified prefix. Its digest is explicitly expected appended bytes, not an independently read content hash.
Final journal failure makes the report INCOMPLETE. Final report/descriptor verification must complete before stdout claims saved evidence.
The fixed native scenario body and the complete original 12-case harness prefix remain unchanged. No source/runtime/policy/workflow or application acceptance is introduced.

limits: A trusted CI output parent remains required. Identity rechecks do not provide atomic protection against every concurrent parent rename.
An empty created artifact or bytes written through a held descriptor can remain after a detected parent mutation. The implementation does not claim to undo those writes.
The digest records verified expected appends. Downloaded journal bytes still require comparison against that digest.
Linux portable verification does not establish Windows ACL, reparse or storage durability properties. Opening with mode 0600 is not proof of a Windows DACL.
